title: The Peopling of the Americas
intro: This passage examines how, when, and by what routes the first human populations entered the Americas, and how newer evidence has unsettled a once-dominant model.

paragraphs.text: The question of how the first humans reached the Americas—continents that, unlike Africa, Europe, and Asia, contained no earlier hominin populations—has occupied archaeologists for more than a century. That the earliest Americans arrived from northeastern Asia is now beyond serious dispute, for both the skeletal anatomy and the genetic makeup of Native American populations point unambiguously to a Siberian origin. The mechanism of their crossing is likewise well understood in outline. During the last glacial maximum, when vast quantities of the planet's water were locked up in continental ice sheets, sea levels fell by more than a hundred meters, exposing a broad plain—known as Beringia—that joined Siberia to Alaska where the Bering Strait now lies. Across this land bridge, and along its shores, the ancestors of the first Americans are thought to have moved eastward, following the game animals on which they depended.

For much of the twentieth century, a single account, often called the Clovis-first model, dominated professional thinking. Named for a site near Clovis, New Mexico, where distinctive fluted stone points were first recognized, the model held that the makers of these tools, arriving roughly 13,000 years ago, were the earliest inhabitants of the hemisphere. According to this reconstruction, the Clovis people entered the interior of North America through a narrow corridor that opened, as the ice sheets began to retreat, between the two great glacial masses covering Canada—the Cordilleran ice of the western mountains and the far larger Laurentide ice to the east. This so-called ice-free corridor, once thought to have served as the sole gateway southward, was for decades treated as the essential precondition for the settlement of the Americas below the ice.

The apparent tidiness of the Clovis-first model concealed a chronological difficulty that would eventually prove fatal to it. Geological and biological studies of the corridor itself indicated that, although a gap between the ice sheets may have existed physically by about 13,000 years ago, the newly deglaciated ground remained for some time a barren expanse of meltwater lakes and bare sediment, devoid of the plants and animals that migrating hunters would have required. ■ A route that could be walked, in other words, was not necessarily a route that could be lived along. ■ This realization prompted a growing number of researchers to look toward an alternative: a migration down the Pacific coast, whose ice-free pockets and rich marine resources—fish, shellfish, seals, and seabirds—could have sustained travelers moving by boat well before the interior corridor became viable. ■ Because the shorelines these coastal migrants would have followed now lie submerged beneath the risen sea, direct archaeological confirmation of the hypothesis has been frustratingly hard to obtain. ■

What ultimately overturned the older consensus was not theory but the accumulation of sites that were simply too old to fit it. The most influential of these is Monte Verde, in southern Chile, where waterlogged soils preserved wooden artifacts, cordage, and even edible plants alongside stone tools. Radiocarbon determinations place the occupation at roughly 14,500 years ago—at least a thousand years before Clovis, and, more tellingly, at the very southern end of a continent whose northern gateway is supposed to have opened later still. Monte Verde was initially met with fierce skepticism; only after a group of prominent critics visited the excavation in person and endorsed its findings did resistance largely collapse. The site's location and antiquity are difficult to reconcile with entry through an interior corridor, and they accord far more readily with an earlier coastal passage.

The picture that has emerged is consequently more complicated, and more provisional, than the one it replaced. Few archaeologists still regard Clovis as marking the first human presence in the Americas, yet no successor model commands comparable authority, and the coastal hypothesis, however plausible, awaits the kind of decisive evidence that its drowned landscapes may never yield. Genetic analyses have introduced further complexity, suggesting that the founding population may have paused for millennia in Beringia before dispersing—a scenario sometimes called the Beringian standstill. If nothing else, the collapse of the Clovis-first orthodoxy illustrates a recurring lesson in archaeology: that an elegant model, precisely because it explains the available evidence so neatly, can discourage the search for the very findings that would eventually undo it.

glossary.def: the land bridge and surrounding region that connected Siberia and Alaska when sea levels were low
a stone spear point with a channel flaked from its base, characteristic of the Clovis culture
a method of estimating the age of organic material from its content of a radioactive form of carbon

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1, what evidence indicates that the earliest Americans came from northeastern Asia?
options: The distribution of game animals across Beringia
Both the skeletal anatomy and the genetics of Native American populations
The height of sea levels during the last glacial maximum
The width of the plain exposed between Siberia and Alaska
questions.explain: 原文：“both the skeletal anatomy and the genetic makeup of Native American populations point unambiguously to a Siberian origin”，即骨骼解剖与遗传两方面共同指向西伯利亚起源。B 正确。A、C、D 都是关于陆桥形成机制的描述，并非证明「来自何处」的证据。

questions.stem: The word "exposing" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to
options: flooding
uncovering
warming
dividing
questions.explain: exposing 在此指海平面下降后使原本被水覆盖的平原「显露、露出」，与 uncovering 同义。原文语境是海平面下降 exposing a broad plain。flooding（淹没）恰好相反；warming、dividing 均无依据。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, the Clovis-first model claimed that the ice-free corridor was
options: the only route by which people could reach the Americas south of the ice
impassable until long after the Clovis people had arrived
located along the Pacific coast of North America
richer in plants and animals than the surrounding regions
questions.explain: 原文：“This so-called ice-free corridor, once thought to have served as the sole gateway southward”——曾被视为南下的唯一通道。A 正确。B 与「roughly 13,000 years ago … the Clovis people entered … through a narrow corridor」矛盾；C 混淆了走廊（内陆）与沿海路线；D 是第 3 段对走廊「barren」的描述的反面。

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the essential information in the highlighted sentence in paragraph 3? Incorrect choices change the meaning or leave out essential information.
questions.highlight: Geological and biological studies of the corridor itself indicated that, although a gap between the ice sheets may have existed physically by about 13,000 years ago, the newly deglaciated ground remained for some time a barren expanse of meltwater lakes and bare sediment, devoid of the plants and animals that migrating hunters would have required.
options: Studies showed that even after the ice sheets parted, the corridor long remained barren and lacked the plants and animals that migrating hunters needed.
Studies proved that the gap between the ice sheets never actually opened, so hunters could not have passed through it.
Geologists found that meltwater lakes made the corridor impossible to cross at any point in its history.
Because migrating hunters required plants and animals, they created the barren landscape found in the deglaciated corridor.
questions.explain: 原句核心：走廊虽在约13,000年前物理上已开通，但很长时间内仍是荒芜之地，缺乏迁徙猎人所需的动植物。A 全部保留。B 编造「gap 从未真正开通」，与「may have existed physically」相反；C 说「任何时期都无法穿越」过度绝对；D 因果颠倒（把猎人当成荒芜的成因）。

questions.stem: The word "viable" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
options: dangerous
usable
visible
narrow
questions.explain: viable 指内陆走廊「变得可用、可行」，与 usable 同义。原文说沿海路线可以在内陆走廊 became viable 之前就维持旅行者，反衬 viable ＝ 具备通行/生存条件。dangerous、visible、narrow 均不合语境。

questions.stem: Look at the four squares [■] in paragraph 3 that indicate where the following sentence could be added. Where would the sentence best fit?
questions.insert_sentence: The chief obstacle to testing it, however, is a matter of geography as much as of evidence.
options: 方块 ①
方块 ②
方块 ③
方块 ④
questions.explain: 待插句用「testing it」回指前句刚提出的 alternative（沿海迁徙假说），并用 however 引出「检验它的主要障碍是地理问题」，恰好领起末句「Because the shorelines … now lie submerged … direct archaeological confirmation … has been frustratingly hard to obtain」对该地理障碍的展开。故放在第 ④ 个方块（末句之前）最合适。放在①②③都会打断「barren → 转向沿海假说 → 资源支撑」的连贯推进。

questions.stem: The word "these" in paragraph 4 refers to
options: sites that were too old to fit the Clovis-first model
the ice sheets covering Canada
radiocarbon determinations
prominent critics of the excavation
questions.explain: these 紧承上一句“the accumulation of sites that were simply too old to fit it”，指「那些年代太早、无法纳入旧模型的遗址」，Monte Verde 是其中「最有影响力的」。A 正确。B、C、D 均非 these 的先行词。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 4, all of the following are true of Monte Verde EXCEPT:
options: Waterlogged soils preserved wooden artifacts and edible plants there.
Its occupation dates to roughly 14,500 years ago, earlier than Clovis.
It lies at the northern gateway through which people are thought to have entered.
It was initially met with strong skepticism by other researchers.
questions.explain: 原文说 Monte Verde 位于智利南部，即「the very southern end of a continent」，与「北方门户」相反，故 C 是与原文冲突的表述（EXCEPT 选它）。A、B、D 分别对应「waterlogged soils preserved wooden artifacts … edible plants」「roughly 14,500 years ago—at least a thousand years before Clovis」「met with fierce skepticism」，均为原文明述。

questions.stem: In paragraph 4, why does the author mention that "a group of prominent critics visited the excavation in person and endorsed its findings"?
questions.highlight: a group of prominent critics visited the excavation in person and endorsed its findings
options: To suggest that the dating of Monte Verde is still widely doubted
To explain how resistance to the site's early date was largely overcome
To prove that the ice-free corridor opened earlier than once believed
To show that critics rarely change their views about controversial sites
questions.explain: 该细节紧跟「Monte Verde was initially met with fierce skepticism; only after…」，说明正是这些著名批评者亲赴现场并认可，才使反对声「largely collapse」。作者借此解释争议如何被平息。B 正确。A 与「resistance largely collapse」相反；C、D 均属曲解，与文意不符。

questions.stem: An introductory sentence for a brief summary of the passage is provided below. Complete the summary by selecting the THREE answer choices that express the most important ideas in the passage.
questions.intro_sentence: Ideas about how and when the first humans reached the Americas have changed substantially as new evidence has accumulated.
options: For decades the Clovis-first model held that people entered the Americas about 13,000 years ago through an ice-free corridor between the Canadian ice sheets, once thought to be the only route south.

Studies of the corridor showed it long remained barren after opening, encouraging support for an alternative migration down the Pacific coast, though submerged shorelines make that route hard to confirm.
Sites too old for the Clovis-first model, above all Monte Verde in southern Chile at about 14,500 years ago, ultimately forced archaeologists to abandon it in favor of a more provisional picture.
Native Americans are now known to have originated in Africa rather than in Siberia, contrary to earlier genetic and skeletal studies.
The Clovis people are thought to have reached southern Chile by boat before the ice-free corridor became passable.
Because the coastal hypothesis has been confirmed by well-preserved shoreline sites, most archaeologists now consider the peopling of the Americas a settled question.
questions.explain: ①克洛维斯第一模型的核心主张——约13,000年前经内陆无冰走廊（曾被视为唯一通道）进入（第2段主旨）；②走廊长期荒芜促成沿海迁徙假说，但海岸线沉没难以证实（第3段主旨）；③Monte Verde 等过早遗址最终迫使学界放弃旧模型、转向更暂定的图景（第4–5段主旨）。干扰项：④原文明确指向西伯利亚起源，非非洲；⑤张冠李戴，把 Monte Verde 的年代/地点安到「克洛维斯人乘船」上，原文未如此说；⑥与末段「awaits the kind of decisive evidence that its drowned landscapes may never yield」及问题仍未定论相反。
